claims.text: HTN: a CCB is preferred over a beta-blocker when angina comes with a bronchospastic disorder, coronary spasm, or Raynaud phenomenon.
claims.quote: A calcium channel blocker is preferred to a beta-blocker in patients with angina pectoris who also have a bronchospastic disorder, with coronary spasms, or with Raynaud phenomenon.

claims.text: Avoid short-acting nifedipine (higher acute MI risk).
claims.quote: Use of short-acting nifedipine should be avoided because of an increased risk of acute myocardial infarction

claims.text: HTN doses: amlodipine start 5 mg once daily, max 10 mg;
claims.quote: Adult recommended starting dose: 5 mg once daily with maximum dose 10 mg once daily.

claims.text: nifedipine ER start 30 or 60 mg once daily;
claims.quote: Therapy for either hypertension or angina should be initiated with 30 or 60 mg once daily.

claims.text: verapamil IR usually starts at 80 mg three times a day (240 mg/day).
claims.quote: The usual initial monotherapy dose in clinical trials was 80 mg three times a day (240 mg/day).

claims.text: Precaution: taper a beta-blocker (don't stop it abruptly) before starting nifedipine.
claims.quote: It is important to taper beta blockers if possible, rather than stopping them abruptly before beginning nifedipine.

claims.text: Counseling: swallow ER nifedipine whole; don't chew, divide or crush it.
claims.quote: PROCARDIA XL Extended Release Tablets should be swallowed whole. Do not chew, divide or crush tablets.

claims.text: Interactions: limit simvastatin to 20 mg/day with amlodipine;
claims.quote: Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily
claims.locator: 7.2 Impact of Amlodipine on Other Drugs

claims.text: with diltiazem, limit simvastatin to 10 mg and diltiazem to 240 mg/day.
claims.quote: If coadministration of simvastatin with diltiazem is required, limit the daily doses of simvastatin to 10 mg and diltiazem to 240 mg.

claims.text: Verapamil can raise digoxin levels 50–75% in the first week;
claims.quote: chronic verapamil treatment can increase serum digoxin levels by 50% to 75% during the first week of therapy

claims.text: monitor digoxin levels when starting, adjusting or stopping diltiazem.
claims.quote: Monitor digoxin levels when initiating, adjusting, and discontinuing diltiazem hydrochloride therapy

claims.text: Avoid grapefruit juice with nifedipine;
claims.quote: Avoid ingestion of grapefruit and grapefruit juice should be avoided while taking nifedipine.

claims.text: it may also raise verapamil levels.
claims.quote: Grapefruit juice may increase plasma levels of verapamil.

claims.text: Avoid CYP3A4 inducers with nifedipine (eg, phenytoin)
claims.quote: Avoid co-administration of nifedipine with phenytoin or any known CYP3A4 inducer

claims.text: and diltiazem (eg, rifampin).
claims.quote: Avoid coadministration of diltiazem with rifampin or any known CYP3A4 inducer.

claims.text: Overdose: DHPs cause marked hypotension, possibly with reflex tachycardia;
claims.quote: Overdosage might be expected to cause excessive peripheral vasodilation with marked hypotension and possibly a reflex tachycardia.

claims.text: non-DHPs cause bradycardia, hypotension and heart block.
claims.quote: Events observed following diltiazem overdose included bradycardia, hypotension, heart block, and cardiac failure.

claims.text: Treat with IV calcium, fluids and pressors;
claims.quote: judicious use of calcium infusion, pressor agents, and fluids

claims.text: atropine or pacing for bradycardia/heart block.
claims.quote: Bradycardia frequently responded favorably to atropine, as did heart block, although cardiac pacing was also frequently utilized to treat heart block.

claims.text: Observe a verapamil overdose for at least 48 h (especially ER).
claims.quote: Treat all verapamil overdoses as serious and maintain observation for at least 48 hours (especially the extended-release formulation)
